profile.reading:
This building, NY3, has its own live CoreSite facility page describing it as a distinct facility "located adjacent to NY2" that "complements" CoreSite's existing NY1 (Manhattan) and NY2 (2 Emerson Lane, Secaucus) data centers, confirming CoreSite itself treats NY3 as a separate, real building rather than marketing filler. However, neither the NY3 facility page nor its spec-sheet landing page states a street number distinct from NY2's: both give "2 Emerson Lane, Secaucus, NJ" as NY3's address as well, and this registry's own geocoded property data for this point independently matches that same address. No square footage, MW capacity, or opening year is published for NY3 specifically. This entry treats NY3's address as shared with NY2 per CoreSite's own site, flagged as needing secondary-source confirmation (county property or utility records) before it can be treated as a fully distinct physical address, rather than guessing a different one.

CoreSite is a subsidiary of American Tower Corporation (NYSE: AMT), which completed its acquisition of CoreSite in late 2021; Stonepeak Partners LP separately acquired roughly 29% of American Tower's US data center business in July 2022, later increased to about 36%. CoreSite's own site describes a total portfolio of 30 data centers across 11 US markets totaling more than 4.8 million square feet, with more than 44,000 customer interconnections and 500-plus connected network providers.

American Tower reported record leasing at CoreSite driving stronger-than-expected second-quarter 2026 results, projecting data-center segment revenue of $1.20 billion to $1.22 billion for full-year 2026, roughly 14.9% growth at the midpoint, and raising its full-year outlook on the strength of that performance; the company also budgeted approximately $695 million in data-center development spending for 2026, funding continued build-out across CoreSite's New York/New Jersey cluster among its other markets.

reading.body:
CoreSite NY3 in Secaucus, New Jersey holds 15 megawatts of IT capacity in a facility completed in late September 2025, making it a confirmed addition to the Northeast's data center footprint rather than a future projection.

The building represents incremental growth within an existing campus. CoreSite operates NY2 on the same Secaucus site, and NY3 is the operator's third facility in this New Jersey location serving the New York metropolitan market. At 138,000 square feet, the building is modest by modern standards for a tier-4 facility, yet the 15 megawatt figure comes corroborated by both trade press and independent aggregators, placing it firmly in the registry as commissioned infrastructure rather than planned capacity.

The delayed completion matters for grid planning. The facility was announced in late 2023 with a target of Q4 2024, but construction extended into September 2025. This slip illustrates how data center projects routinely miss initial timelines, affecting the pace at which compute capacity can actually reach market and the grid connections those facilities require.

The data does not reveal what workloads this facility serves, its power source, or whether its 15 megawatts represents full utilization or available headroom. It also does not address whether CoreSite's third Secaucus building absorbed demand that would otherwise have required a new campus location, or whether it reflects genuine regional growth in compute demand.
